decisions.reason: The source changes the component-tier selection policy for the integrated design but does not alter the existing power-board BOM completeness, LCSC-number, or justification obligations.
Choosing Advanced components when Basic alternatives are unavailable does not change the requirement to provide a complete and board-correct sensor-board BOM.
The component sourcing-tier decision does not change the already established single-board architecture or board count.
The source does not change the required sensor modules, external connector fanout, connector types, signals, or absence of interboard connectors.
The JLCPCB Basic-versus-Advanced sourcing policy does not affect whether the specified KiCad footprint resolves portably.
Component sourcing tier has no necessary effect on the QR-code marking requirement.
The decision to permit Advanced components does not modify the lead-free production requirement.
The source concerns sourcing policy for the new integrated design and does not change the legacy main-board BOM or its optional connector-population rule.
The component-tier choice does not change the required sensor-board fabrication and placement export artifacts.
The source supplies SMD-versus-through-hole pricing but does not select either connector assembly style; the decision to use Advanced components is a separate sourcing-tier choice.
The component sourcing-tier decision does not resolve the battery-label ambiguity or alter the connector pin-marking requirement.
The source does not change the legacy interboard connector partition, connector types, pinouts, or power-distribution semantics.
